hints: Use $\cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta$, expand, and collect powers of $\sin\theta$.
Simplify until the expression matches the right-hand side exactly.
walkthrough:
Apply the double angle formula for cosine, $\cos 2A = 2\cos^2 A - 1$, to rewrite $\cos 4\theta = \cos(2(2\theta))$:
$$\cos 4\theta = 2\cos^2 2\theta - 1$$

Substitute $\cos 4\theta$ into the left-hand side of the proposed identity:
$$\cos 4\theta - 4\cos 2\theta = (2\cos^2 2\theta - 1) - 4\cos 2\theta = 2\cos^2 2\theta - 4\cos 2\theta - 1$$

Use the double angle formula in terms of sine, $\cos 2\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta$, to express $\cos 2\theta$ and $\cos^2 2\theta$ in terms of $\sin\theta$:
$$\cos^2 2\theta = (1 - 2\sin^2\theta)^2 = 1 - 4\sin^2\theta + 4\sin^4\theta$$

Substitute these into the quadratic expression:
$$2(1 - 4\sin^2\theta + 4\sin^4\theta) - 4(1 - 2\sin^2\theta) - 1$$
The left-hand side is identically equal to the right-hand side, establishing the identity.

hints: Move $4\cos2\theta$ to the left and use the identity from part (i).

walkthrough:
Rearrange the equation $\cos 4\theta = 4\cos 2\theta + 3$ by moving the cosine term to the left-hand side:
$$\cos 4\theta - 4\cos 2\theta = 3$$

Substitute the identity established in part (i), replacing the left-hand side with $8\sin^4\theta - 3$:
$$8\sin^4\theta - 3 = 3$$

Take the fourth root on both sides:
$$\sin\theta = \pm\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^{1/4} = \pm(0.75)^{0.25} \approx \pm 0.930605$$

Determine all solutions in the interval $0^\circ \leq \theta \leq 360^\circ$ across all four quadrants:
Quadrant 1: $\theta_1 = \alpha = 68.5^\circ$
Quadrant 2: $\theta_2 = 180^\circ - 68.530^\circ = 111.470^\circ \approx 111.5^\circ$
Quadrant 3: $\theta_3 = 180^\circ + 68.530^\circ = 248.530^\circ \approx 248.5^\circ$
Quadrant 4: $\theta_4 = 360^\circ - 68.530^\circ = 291.470^\circ \approx 291.5^\circ$

State all four solutions in ascending order correct to 1 decimal place:
$$\theta = 68.5^\circ, \quad 111.5^\circ, \quad 248.5^\circ, \quad 291.5^\circ$$
